# Draft:Occupational life of the Tribes of Medieval period

The Tribes of the Medieval period can be grouped according to their occupation. However, this is not easy because the tribes earned their Livelihood in a variety of ways. A single tribe could be engaged in different economic activities too.
Hunters and Gatherers
Some tribes like the Chenchu people, Yenadis, Kadar people, Cholanaikkan, Malappandaram tribe, Jenu Kuruba in India, Inuit in the Arctic survived just by hunting and gathering food.
Shifting Cultivators
Tribes such as Gondi people, Ahom people, Bonda people, and the Baiga people were engaged in Shifting cultivation or also known as Jhum cultivation. The tribe cleared a plot of land, cut and burnt the trees, sowed the seeds in ashes, and then cultivated it. When the fertility of the land dropped, they moved onto another plot of land.
Settled Cultivators
The Bhil, Santal people and Munda people, Jats, Cheros, and more gave up their previous Nomadic lifestyle and became Farmers.
Artisans
The Banjaras, Nat people, Koli people are some artisans. These tribes would exchange their craftwork for agricultural products and other necessities. The Kota people (India) of Nigiris sell their woven craftwork in this manner even today.
Pastoralists and Cattle Herders
They moved from one place to other with their animals. They lived on Milk, Meat and other pastoral products and exchanged items such as Wool and Butter with Settled agriculturalists for Grain, Cloth, and other products. Many of the pastoral tribes reared and sold animals such as Cattle and Horses as well. The Gujjars were pastoral tribes who settled down to become cultivators and landowners during this period.
Trader-Nomads
They were an important tribe called Banjaras. They moved with their families. They traded mostly Foodstuff. They carried large loads of goods from one place to another in caravans called tanda. They brought most of their things from Peasants and then went to the urban centers to sell them. Alauddin Khalji used the services of the Banjaras to transport grain to the city markets. They also transported grain for the Mughal army during Military campaigns.
Folk Artistes
They made their living by Acting, Entertaining, and performing in different villages and towns. But there were also groups like the Pardhan people who were the official Genealogists of the Gondi people. They recorded the history of various Gond lines orally, mostly in the form of Songs.
